narrative:
The 2026 Miami Marlins have been a team of extremes, lurching between stunning highs and gut-wrenching lows across a season that has defied easy categorization. They opened with a promising 4-1 March, fueled by Owen Caissie's jaw-dropping walk-off blast on Opening Weekend, before reality hit hard in April and May, when the roster's thin margins were exposed by a string of late-inning collapses — many of them at the hands of a shaky Pete Fairbanks, whose blown saves became a recurring and painful theme.

Just when the season looked destined for irrelevance, June arrived and rewrote everything. The Marlins posted an extraordinary 20-6 record that month, one of the best single-month runs in recent franchise history, as young contributors like Javier Sanoja and Xavier Edwards caught fire and the lineup finally strung together the kind of consistent production it had only hinted at earlier. That summer surge vaulted Miami into genuine relevance and gave the ballpark an electricity it had not felt in years.

The back half of the season has been a grind. July and August brought the Marlins back to earth, with bullpen implosions — a three-run Contreras home run off Fairbanks, a Jarren Duran grand slam off Cade Gibson — repeatedly erasing hard-fought leads. Yet the offense showed resilience, with Heriberto Hernández, Joe Mack, and Javier Sanoja delivering timely hits that kept Miami from fully unraveling. The team never recaptured the June magic, but it never stopped competing either.

Now in September at 80-82, the Marlins find themselves in familiar but uncomfortable territory — mathematically alive but needing help, fighting through a month that has produced both a Sanoja clutch double and a crushing Corbin Carroll home run off Jack Ralston. The final chapter of this season is still being written, and Miami's young core is determined to make it worth reading.

chapters.title: Opening Fireworks
chapters.description: Caissie's Opening Weekend blast ignites early promise in a strong 4-1 March.

chapters.title: April Turbulence
chapters.description: The Marlins' 11-15 April is defined by late-inning heartbreak and Fairbanks blowups offsetting flashes of offensive life.

chapters.title: The June Explosion
chapters.description: A remarkable 20-6 June transforms the Marlins from also-rans into legitimate contenders.

chapters.title: Summer Grind
chapters.description: July and August test Miami's resolve as bullpen collapses and roster limits bring the team back to .500 territory.

chapters.title: September Stakes
chapters.description: With their season on the line, the Marlins fight pitch by pitch through a tense September that could still define everything.
